title: Washroom finishing order and standard
audience: Cleaners who service washrooms in offices, shared buildings, rental properties and short-stay sites.
learningOutcomes: Set out the washroom in the correct working order so that finished surfaces are not re-soiled.
Describe what a finished washroom should look and smell like before you sign it off.
Explain why the floor is left until last and why drains are run with water at the end.

instruction.heading: Why the order matters in a washroom
instruction.body: A washroom is judged quickly. Users notice odour first, then residue on the taps, streaks on the mirror and dust on the high points. Most of these faults come from doing the work in the wrong order. If you wipe a basin and then dust a ceiling vent above it, the falling dust lands on the clean basin. If you mop before you have finished the fixtures, splashes and drips land on a floor you have just cleaned. A fixed sequence lets each surface be finished once, with the dirty work done before the clean work.

instruction.heading: Set up and restock before you touch a surface
instruction.body: Begin by stocking the consumables: toilet paper, paper towel, soap and sanitiser. Replace the bag in the bin and remove any waste. Doing this first means you are not reaching back into the washroom with soiled gloves after you have cleaned the fixtures. Carry the supplies in on a caddy so the chemicals you need are within reach. Put out a 'cleaning in progress' sign or a wet floor sign by the door before you begin, so people know the room is being serviced.

instruction.heading: Dust high, clean wet, end with the floor
instruction.body: Work from the high points down. Reach vents and fittings with an extension duster on vents, light fittings, the tops of partitions and the corners where cobwebs collect. Then move to the basin and counter, cleaning the bowl and the surrounding surfaces with a cloth that has been wetted with an approved cleaner. Polish the mirror and the taps last, because the wet work will mark them. Clean the toilet exterior, seat, hinges, flush control and the base, then the interior of the bowl. Clean the touchpoints, meaning door handles, dispenser buttons and light switches, before the floor. The floor is the final stage, so that anything that falls during the earlier work is caught and removed.

instruction.heading: Drains and the finished standard
instruction.body: Floor drains that are not used regularly can lose the water seal in their trap, which lets odour rise into the room. Run clean water through each floor drain once the job is complete to keep the seal in place. After that, check the finished washroom against the standard: no dust or cobwebs on vents, corners, partitions or lights; no residue on the hinges, flush control or the base of the toilet; mirrors clear of streaks; dispensers full; and no odour. If any of these checks fails, correct it before you leave.

procedure: Place a 'cleaning in progress' or wet floor sign by the entrance and let people know you are working in the washroom.
Put on gloves and eye protection before you open any chemical.
Stock paper products and soap, and replace the bin liner after removing waste.
Dust the high points and corners with an extension duster, working from the far side of the room toward the door.
Clean the basin, counter and surrounds with an approved cleaner on a clean cloth, then wipe the mirror.
Clean the toilet exterior, seat, hinges, flush control and base, and then the bowl.
Clean the touchpoints: door handles, dispenser buttons and light switches.
Polish the taps and any bright metal last, using a dry cloth.
Vacuum or sweep the floor, then run clean water through each floor drain.
Clean and store the equipment, return the caddy, and check the finished standard before you leave.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner in a small office washroom mops the floor first, then dusts the ceiling vent and notices that the dust has landed on the new wet floor and on the freshly polished mirror.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner have done differently, and what needs to happen now?
workedExamples.reasoning: The floor should have been left until after the dusting and the wet work. Now the mirror and the floor need the dust removed and the floor may need a second pass once it has dried. The lesson for the next visit is to dust high points first and leave the floor until last.

workedExamples.situation: At the end of a shift, a cleaner notices a smell coming from a floor drain in a rarely used washroom, although the remainder of the room is clean.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the most likely cause, and what is the correct action?
workedExamples.reasoning: A drain that is not used often may have lost its water seal, so odour can rise through it. Run clean water through the drain as part of the finishing sequence, and report the drain to the supervisor if the smell remains after it has been run.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves suitable for the chemicals in use.
Safety glasses to protect against splashes and spray.
Extension duster and a cloth for high points.
Colour-coded microfiber cloths, one set for each zone.
Approved washroom cleaner and disinfectant, with labels and safety data sheets available.
Toilet brush and a separate brush for the drains if the site uses one.
'Cleaning in progress' sign or wet floor sign.
Caddy or cart stocked with paper products and soap.
Vacuum or dust pan and broom for the floor.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the floor before the fixtures and high points are finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the set order: restock, dust high, clean wet, polish, then floor last.

commonErrors.error: Touching the face or hair with gloves on, or pulling gloves off with a bare hand.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep hands away from the face, especially the eyes and mouth, and remove gloves carefully when finished.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the drains, which leaves an odour that returns after the room has been cleaned.
commonErrors.prevention: Make running water through floor drains a fixed final step on every washroom job.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wear gloves and eye protection when cleaning and when handling chemicals. Keep hands away from the face while working.
Never mix cleaning chemicals. Use one product at a time, rinse between products, and read the label before use.
Your state or territory's work health and safety requirements apply to washroom work. This lesson does not set those requirements out in full.

qualityStandard: No dust or cobwebs are visible on vents, corners, partitions or light fittings.
No residue or residue is visible on hinges, the flush control or the base of the toilet.
Mirrors show no streaks and the taps are polished.
Dispensers are stocked and the bin liner is replaced.
The floor is clean and the floor drains have been run with water.
The room has no odour once the job is complete.
documentationEvidence: Job record showing the washroom was serviced and the date and time.
Note of any stock that was low or missing, and any fixture that needs repair.
Note of any floor drain that still smelled after it was run.
summary: The order of work prevents fixtures and floors from being re-soiled.
Restock first, dust high points, clean wet surfaces, polish last, and end with the floor.
Run water through floor drains at the end to keep odour out of the room.
Check the room against the finished standard before you sign it off.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the washroom finishing standard leave the floor for last?
options: Because the floor is the easiest surface to dry afterwards and the mop water dries fastest
So that dust and drips from earlier work are caught and removed by the final floor clean
So that the drains are run before the fixtures are cleaned and the taps are dried last

knowledgeChecks.question: A washroom has a smell only near one floor drain. What is the most likely cause, and what should be done?
options: A blocked toilet, so pour strong chemical into the bowl and leave it overnight to act on the blockage
Dirty mirrors near the drain, so polish them again first and wipe the drain cover with a damp cloth
A dry trap that has lost its water seal, so run clean water through the drain and report it if the smell stays

knowledgeChecks.question: Which action belongs at the start of the washroom job, before any surface is cleaned?
options: Putting on gloves and eye protection, and setting out a sign at the entrance
Polishing the taps using a dry cloth and the chrome around the sink
Running water through the floor drains and then the toilet lid and seat
